# libffi (vendored) — provenance and regeneration

- **Upstream:** https://github.com/libffi/libffi
- **Version pin:** v3.4.8 (release tarball `libffi-3.4.8.tar.gz`)
- **Tarball sha256:** `bc9842a18898bfacb0ed1252c4febcc7e78fa139fd27fdc7a3e30d9d9356119b`
- **License:** MIT — `LICENSE` in this directory is upstream's, shipped verbatim.
  Fits the vendoring policy (small, MIT, yyjson precedent).

## Vendoring shape (the decision)

**Pruned tree with per-target generated configs COMMITTED** — not the full autoconf
source drop. Rationale: openq is a plain-Makefile, zero-dependency build; libffi's
configure step exists to (a) pick the port sources and (b) generate `ffi.h` +
`fficonfig.h`. Both are fully determined by our two fixed targets, so we ran configure
once per target at vendoring time and committed the outputs. No autoconf, libtool, or
configure runs at build time, ever.

- `src/`, `include/` — upstream sources, verbatim, pruned to the two ports we build
  (x86-64 SysV + x86-64 win64, closures included). `dlmalloc.c` is textually
  `#include`d by `closures.c`, never compiled standalone.
- `config/linux-x86_64/` — `ffi.h` + `fficonfig.h` generated by configure on
  linux x86-64 gcc.
- `config/win64/` — the same pair generated with `--host=x86_64-w64-mingw32`.

Port source split (mirrors upstream `configure.host`):

| TU | linux | win64 |
|---|---|---|
| `src/prep_cif.c` `src/types.c` `src/closures.c` `src/tramp.c` | yes | yes |
| `src/x86/ffiw64.c` + `src/x86/win64.S` | yes (EFI64 entry points) | yes |
| `src/x86/ffi64.c` + `src/x86/unix64.S` | yes | no (SysV-only) |

Static trampolines are DISABLED on both targets (`--disable-exec-static-tramp`):
closures use the classic mmap/VirtualAlloc path. `src/tramp.c` still compiles (both
targets) because `closures.c` calls `ffi_tramp_*` unconditionally — with the feature
off it compiles to the stub bodies in its `#else` arm.

## Regeneration recipe (version bump or new target)

```sh
curl -LO https://github.com/libffi/libffi/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/libffi-X.Y.Z.tar.gz
tar xzf libffi-X.Y.Z.tar.gz && cd libffi-X.Y.Z
CFG="--disable-shared --enable-static --disable-docs \
     --disable-multi-os-directory --disable-exec-static-tramp"
mkdir b-linux && (cd b-linux && ../configure $CFG)
mkdir b-win   && (cd b-win   && ../configure --host=x86_64-w64-mingw32 $CFG)
# then copy:
#   LICENSE, include/{ffi_common.h,ffi_cfi.h,tramp.h}
#   src/{prep_cif.c,types.c,closures.c,tramp.c,dlmalloc.c}
#   src/x86/{ffi64.c,ffiw64.c,unix64.S,win64.S,internal.h,internal64.h,asmnames.h,ffitarget.h}
#   b-linux/include/ffi.h + b-linux/fficonfig.h -> config/linux-x86_64/
#   b-win/include/ffi.h   + b-win/fficonfig.h   -> config/win64/
# record the new tarball sha256 above; no local patches — tree is verbatim upstream.
```

A new target (e.g. aarch64) = one more configure run, one more `config/<target>/`
pair, plus that port's `src/<arch>/` sources and a Makefile arm.

The Makefile gates all libffi objects on a `Linux-x86_64` host (native build and the
win64 cross both run there): other hosts — macOS arm64 in the release matrix — keep
building WITHOUT libffi until their port is vendored per the recipe above.

Build cost: 9 TUs, ~1.25s cold serial compile (gcc -O0, ccache off) — noise in a
full build on both targets.
